name: Abeid Amani Karume International Airport
before:
Zanzibar's airport, on Unguja Island about 5 km south of Zanzibar City, with flights across East Africa and out to Europe and the Middle East.

Which terminal a client uses is worth checking. Terminal 3 handles international flights and Terminal 2 takes domestic plus some international, so a connecting passenger may have to move between buildings. Terminal 1, the small one from the British protectorate era, is no longer used for flights and is now the airport office.

Terminal 3 was a long time coming. Work started in January 2011, it was expected in 2014, and financial and technical delays pushed the opening to September 2020, with flights from early 2021. It came with a new apron of 100,000 square metres, replacing one of 21,000, and lifted capacity to 1.5 million passengers a year.

The airport was previously called Kisauni and then Zanzibar International, and was renamed in 2010 after Abeid Amani Karume, the island's first president.
after:
Zanzibar's main airport, on Unguja Island south of Zanzibar City, with flights across East Africa and out to Europe and the Middle East.

Check which terminal a client's flight uses, particularly for a connection. Terminal 3 is the international terminal. A new Terminal 2 was nearly finished in August 2026, and a bridge between the terminal buildings is being built. Terminal 1 has been refurbished for VIP and private flights.

The airport is named after Abeid Amani Karume, Zanzibar's first president.

Whether it has opened, and which flights it takes, is not confirmed, hence the advice to check.
